mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS is in the lowest quartile of its historical range is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a monetary policy easing cycle coinciding with a tightening labor market, which together boost economic growth and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market tightening
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction term (FEDFUNDS change * UNRATE change) and 60-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 60-day return when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE decline is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-demand regime (RSAFS > 450,000), a rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures that prompt monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when RSAFS > 450000, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns (conditional on RSAFS > 450000) is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between INDPRO and 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the average 5-day return when INDPRO is rising is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts rate (HOUST) exceeding 1.2 million units signals strong consumer demand for housing and related sectors, boosting economic growth and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1.2 million units, or the Rank IC between HOUST and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates broad-based economic strength across both consumer and manufacturing sectors, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST change * INDPRO change) and 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when both HOUST and INDPRO rise is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), a rising employment level (PAYEMS) signals sustained labor market strength that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC between PAYEMS and 5-day returns (conditional on UNRATE < 4.0%) is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
